card.name: Just before rare-event reporting phrases
card.fires_on: Small words or punctuation right after a serious adverse event, where the next words are likely to say it was reported or has occurred, e.g. 'have been reported'. Also hedging commas before 'theoretically'.

modes.label: Before 'been reported'
modes.description: The auxiliary verb or word after a severe outcome, just ahead of 'been reported' or 'been associated'.
modes.example: Acute liver failure requiring transplantation<< has>> been reported in the postmarketing setting.

modes.label: Closing a list of events
modes.description: A closing parenthesis or noun after a list of conditions, before 'have also been reported'.
modes.example: Autoimmune disorders (such as Graves’ disease, polymyositis, and Guillain-Barré syndrome<<)>> have also been reported to occur in the

modes.label: Hedge before rare risk
modes.description: A comma or 'in' that introduces a qualifier such as 'in some cases' or 'theoretically'.
modes.example: This product is made from human plasma and may contain infectious agents, e.g. viruses and<<,>> theoretically, the Creutzfeldt-J

card.writes: It pushes toward words meaning rare or occasional and away from words meaning often.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a label is about to say a serious effect has rarely been reported.
